articles.headline: Lions lose DB Avonte Maddox for season; Dan Campbell defends DC
articles.description: The embattled Lions defense has lost defensive back Avonte Maddox for the season, while coach Dan Campbell is defending second-year defensive coordinator Kelvin Sheppard.
articles.body:
ALLEN PARK, Mich. -- The embattled Detroit Lions defense has lost a key piece of the secondary for the season, while coach Dan Campbell is defending second-year defensive coordinator Kelvin Sheppard.

Lions defensive back Avonte Maddox will miss the remainder of the season after suffering a foot injury that requires surgery, Campbell announced Monday.

Campbell, meanwhile, defended Sheppard, whose defense has given up 71 points through the first two weeks of the season.

"I believe in Sheppard. I believe he's an outstanding coach. There's a bump in the road," Campbell said. "I think this staff is outstanding. That defensive staff.

"It's a veteran staff, and I think they're versatile and we've got to coach better -- and they can coach better, I can coach better, but I believe they're the right guys to get this thing done."

This Sunday, the Lions (1-1) host the New York Jets, coached by Aaron Glenn, whom Sheppard succeeded as the Lions' defensive coordinator.

Maddox was hurt during the first half of Thursday night's 41-31 loss to the Buffalo Bills, getting carted off the field and ruled out in the inaugural regular-season game at Highmark Stadium. He went down after a second-quarter collision with teammate Chuck Clark in the end zone and limped off the field next to team trainers before going to the locker room on a cart.

"That hurts a little bit. Maddox is a good player for us. A good solid football player. I hate that for him," Campbell said. "That's the hand we're dealt, and we move forward."

The Lions are also missing starting safeties Brian Branch (Achilles) and Kerby Joseph (knee), who are on the physically unable to perform list and still must miss at least the next two games.

Campbell said they won't return to practice this week, with no clear timetable set for either player to return, but Branch could return sooner than Joseph -- whose chronic knee injury continues to linger.

"I just know we were strengthening the knee, and it wasn't a setback, but there was a little time there where we weren't able to do everything we needed to do and so now, we're back at it," Campbell said of Joseph. "And until we can get the knee to a certain point to where it feels strong, as strong as we can possibly get it and he feels comfortable, we're not gonna put him out there until he's ready."

With Detroit's defense depleted in the secondary, it is looking to add help immediately. The Lions hosted a group of free agents for a Monday workout, sources told ESPN's Jeremy Fowler. Among the veterans attending were Jordan Fuller, Jalen Mills and Mike Edwards, sources said.

The Lions' defense couldn't stop the Bills, allowing 446 yards and 34 first downs while forcing just two punts. That continues a trend from Week 1 as the Detroit defense has allowed 63 first downs this season, which is tied for the second most all time through two games, per ESPN Research.

articles.headline: J.K. Dobbins, RJ Harvey injured; Broncos' run game in question
articles.description: With injuries to J.K. Dobbins and RJ Harvey, the Denver Broncos are looking at the week ahead before determining which running back will be ready for Sunday night's game against the Los Angeles Rams.
articles.body:
ENGLEWOOD, Colo. - Denver Broncos coach Sean Payton's back issues have flared up again, but his team's injury questions at running back may be a bigger pain this week.

J.K. Dobbins, who leads the team in carries (18) and rushing yards (72) after two games, and RJ Harvey each have hamstring injuries that make them question marks for Sunday night's game against the Los Angeles Rams.

Payton said Monday "I think there's a lot ahead of us this week in regards to who our runners are going to be.'' Rookie Jonah Coleman, who had 33 of his 39 yards rushing in Sunday's win over the Jacksonville Jaguars on the game-closing drive, could be pushed to the front of the backfield rotation.

Dobbins left Sunday's game in the third quarter with a left hamstring injury and Harvey was a gameday inactive due to a hamstring injury he suffered in the season-opening loss in Kansas City. Overall, the team has continued to search for an identity in its offense, particularly in the run game.

An inconsistency that included a possession against the Jaguars, when the Broncos faced a first-and-goal from the Jacksonville 1-yard line, and had three carries from Dobbins that went for no gain, no gain and a loss of a yard. The Broncos ended up with Wil Lutz kicking a 20-yard field goal.

"It wasn't anything good,'' Payton said. " ... I would say just overall a real bad possession,''

The Rams, who play the New York Giants Monday night, surrendered 122 yards rushing to the 49ers in their season opener. In addition to Coleman the Broncos have Tyler Badie on their active roster to go with Cody Schrader on their practice squad.

articles.headline: Sauce Gardner's journey with Colts is stuck in a 9-game rut
articles.description: The Colts are off to an 0-2 start, which doesn't bode well for the front office, and doesn't sit well with the players.
articles.body:
INDIANAPOLIS -- Sauce Gardner's New York Jets lost 66% of their games during his tenure with the club from 2022 to Week 9 of 2025. It was a cascade of misery, with New York posting the fourth-worst record in the NFL during that period (20-39).

It's why Gardner, a former All-Pro cornerback, was so eager to join the Indianapolis Colts when he was traded midway through last season. In a remarkable shift, he found himself playing a key role for the team with the best record in the NFL at the time (7-2).

These days, things couldn't be more different.

The Colts won their first game following the trade, and they haven't won since. The losing continued Sunday night with a 33-30 overtime loss to the Kansas City Chiefs.

"It doesn't sit good," Gardner said. "I'd be lying if I told you it did. We've got to turn it around.

"It's definitely something that I was excited about. Excited to win, expecting to win. When I got here, like I said, we've got the guys, we've got the players, we've got the coaches. We've just got to actually win when the clock hits zero, zero. It's definitely crazy, though."

The Colts are on a nine-game losing streak that dates back to a Week 12 loss to Kansas City last season, also in overtime. That was the start of a season-ending seven-game losing streak due, in part, to a rash of injuries.

But, now, even with quarterback Daniel Jones back from his Achilles tear, Gardner mostly healthy (he was injured off and on late last season) and veteran defensive tackle DeForest Buckner recovered from neck surgery, little has changed.

No team has a longer current losing streak than Indianapolis (0-2).

Pressure is mounting.

"We are right there," coach Shane Steichen said. "We have to find a way to win at the end. That was one of those games. It is a freaking harda-- league, and you have got to find a way to win these tight games."

The backdrop behind all of this is the intense scrutiny on Steichen, general manager Chris Ballard and many of the veteran players. Extensive changes and firings are considered likely if the Colts don't show improvement in 2026. Owner Carlie Irsay-Gordon is on record saying that expectations of progress are in place during this, her second full season as the team's primary leader alongside her two sisters.

Steichen has a 25-28 record since his hiring in 2023 and the Colts haven't made the playoffs since 2020. They haven't won the AFC South since 2014, three years before Ballard was hired.

Now, in Year 10 under Ballard, the Colts find themselves with a defense that is off to a historically poor start. Just one team in NFL history has allowed more total yardage in Weeks 1 and 2 than the Colts' 1,023 yards. The 2016 Oakland Raiders allowed 1,035 yards. Indianapolis has allowed more than 500 yards of offense in each of its two games this season.

All of which makes winning unlikely. Winning is a feeling the Colts haven't tasted in far too long.

articles.headline: Kylian Mbappé refuses to criticise referee despite Madrid derby 'mistakes'
articles.description: Kylian Mbappé has refused to criticise the referee in charge of Real Madrid's 2-1 derby defeat to Atlético Madrid, despite admitting that official Miguel Ángel Ortiz Arias made "mistakes" in his handling of the match.
articles.body:
Kylian Mbappé has refused to criticise the referee in charge of Real Madrid's 2-1 derby defeat to Atlético Madrid, despite admitting that official Miguel Ángel Ortiz Arias made "mistakes" in his handling of the match.

Madrid coach José Mourinho claimed on Sunday that Ortiz Arias had failed to show "two clear red cards" for rough, first-half challenges by Kang-in Lee and Cristian Romero, bringing a printout with photos of the incidents into his post-game news conference.

The result left Madrid six points behind LaLiga leaders Barcelona with just seven games played going into the international break -- with a Clásico to come at Camp Nou in October -- leaving Mourinho under pressure already in his second spell at the Bernabéu.

"I don't think I've ever been a player who talks much about referees," Mbappé told Diario AS in an interview in Switzerland, where he has agreed a new sponsorship deal with the brand On.

"I'm not going to start now. I have my own thoughts, but I'll keep them to myself... Referees are human, they make mistakes -- and those were mistakes -- but I don't want to get into that."

Romero was shown a yellow card for treading on Jude Bellingham's knee -- after a VAR check, when Bellingham had initially been cautioned for the clash -- while Lee escaped punishment for a high boot on Federico Valverde's ankle.

Atlético then went ahead in the second half at the Metropolitano through Alejandro Grimaldo's penalty after Dean Huijsen had been sent off, before Jonathan David made it 2-0, and then Antonio Rüdiger pulled a late goal back for Madrid.

It's a second defeat for Mourinho's side this season, after losing 1-0 at Real Betis earlier this month.

Atlético clapped back on Monday with three social media posts mocking Mourinho for bringing the printouts to the post-match conference. 

The first shows a printer as it releases a copy of a page with a photo of Mourinho and a caption that says: "Stop referee harassment now." 

"[It's] a step backwards," Mbappé said, when asked about the derby loss. "It's very tough, we wanted to win, and we knew what kind of game it would be.

"But the team gave everything, and we're moving forward, because there's still a long way to go this season, and we have to stay on the right track... We have to work, and do more. We have to put the work in."

Mbappé will now join up for international duty with France under new coach Zinedine Zidane, who was one of the forward's childhood idols.

Zidane -- who has replaced long-term boss Didier Deschamps -- was working behind-the-scenes at Madrid when Mbappé first went on trial to the Spanish capital as a youngster.

articles.headline: Clippers name lawyer John Gibson interim governor
articles.description: Los Angeles-based trial lawyer John Gibson will serve as the Clippers' interim governor. He will take over for Steve Ballmer, who has been suspended one year following an investigation into salary cap circumvention.
articles.body:
The LA Clippers have named John Gibson, a Los Angeles-based trial lawyer, as the franchise's interim governor and CEO.

Clippers owner Steve Ballmer, who is facing a one-year suspension following the NBA's investigation into salary cap circumvention allegations involving the team's former star Kawhi Leonard, nominated Gibson, and the NBA approved him Monday after a vetting process.

Gibson is a longtime Clippers season-ticket holder and, along with being a trial lawyer, was a litigation partner at DLA Piper in Los Angeles. He is a graduate of Harvard and the University of Michigan Law School.

"I am honored to take on this responsibility and grateful for the opportunity to serve an organization I have supported for many years," Gibson said in a statement.

Gibson joins the Clippers nearly three weeks after the NBA handed down its harshest-ever punishment to the team following a nearly yearlong investigation by the law firm Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz. Along with Ballmer's suspension, the NBA issued a $30 million fine, the forfeiture of five first-round draft picks and suspensions for team executives Lawrence Frank and Gillian Zucker.

Leonard was also fined $700,000.

Ballmer recently accepted the NBA's punishment, saying in a statement, in part, that though there are still disagreements with the findings, "We are complying with the penalties assessed by the league, have paid the fine and are moving forward."

articles.headline: Bears' Johnson: QB Williams week-to-week, likely to miss time
articles.description: Bears coach Ben Johnson said Monday on ESPN 1000 that quarterback Caleb Williams' right hamstring injury "sounds like it's going to be a week-to-week deal for him."
articles.body:
CHICAGO -- Bears quarterback Caleb Williams is considered "week-to-week" with a right hamstring injury he sustained in a 9-3 loss to the Minnesota Vikings, coach Ben Johnson said Monday morning.

During an appearance on ESPN 1000, Johnson said he anticipates Williams will be sidelined for "some time."

"It sounds like it's going to be a week-to-week deal for him," Johnson said. "I've got to still talk with our trainer. We'll do that here shortly and I'll have the lowdown from him. But it sounds like it's week-to-week but will likely miss some time."

Williams underwent an MRI on Monday morning to assess the severity of his hamstring injury.

Johnson was noncommittal when asked whether he felt the Bears had dodged a bullet with the extent of Williams' injury not being more severe.

"Yeah, potentially," Johnson said. "Potentially. You know, we'll see. He's tough and he comes back from these types of things, I think, better than the average human being. So, we'll see."

Johnson will speak to local reporters Monday afternoon.

articles.headlineJa: NBA全チームの2026-27シーズンを左右する可能性のあるスタッツ
articles.descriptionJa: NBAのシーズンを決定づける可能性のあるトレンド、ストーリーライン、注目のスタッツ情報に迫る。
articles.body:
One of my favorite annual preseason traditions is to identify one number for every NBA team, sourced from a variety of data points and statistical categories, that highlights a key aspect of each squad entering the new season.

Last year, for instance, this exercise foreshadowed Jalen Johnson's breakout in Atlanta, the Milwaukee Bucks' struggles in Giannis Antetokounmpo's final season and the Portland Trail Blazers' league-worst turnover rate.

Let's dive into this year's 30 numbers to get a sense for the 2026-27 season to come, featuring all sorts of trends, storylines and statistical nuggets to monitor over the next 10 months.

Jump to a team:

ATL | BOS | BKN | CHA | CHI | CLE

DAL | DEN | DET | GS | HOU | IND

LAC | LAL | MEM | MIA | MIL | MIN

NO | NY | OKC | ORL | PHI | PHX

POR | SAC | SA | TOR | UTAH | WAS

Atlanta Hawks: 108.6

The Hawks allowed just 108.6 points per 100 possessions after the All-Star break, ranking second in the NBA in that span, behind only the Oklahoma City Thunder.

Over the whole season, the Hawks ranked 10th on defense -- and that was before they added Luguentz Dort, one of the most ferocious perimeter defenders in the NBA. Whether Dort and Dyson Daniels can survive on offense if and when they play together remains to be seen, but that duo with Nickeil Alexander-Walker plus Atlanta's other defensive infrastructure could combine to form one of the NBA's stingiest units.

Boston Celtics: 4

In all four of Joe Mazzulla's seasons as Boston's head coach, the Celtics have finished with a top-five offensive and defensive rating, per Cleaning the Glass. Only three other squads in that span have accomplished that feat: the 2023-24 Thunder, the 2024-25 Thunder and the 2025-26 San Antonio Spurs.

That consistent two-way excellence hasn't always translated to the playoffs. In those four seasons, Boston won one title but was upset in the other three years

Yet after an offseason of turmoil, that consistency should also be encouraging for Celtics fans. Even without Jaylen Brown, their team will likely look like a championship contender on both sides once again -- in the regular season, at least.

Brooklyn Nets: 72%

Egor Demin was by far the best of the Nets' rookies last season, averaging 10.3 points per game and a solid assist-to-turnover ratio while making 38.5% of his 3-pointers. That latter statistic is especially encouraging for a player with shooting questions entering the NBA.

But Demin didn't find many ways to score other than 3-pointers, as 72% of his shot attempts last season were 3s. That was the 16th-highest rate out of 279 players with at least 1,000 minutes last season -- the three players immediately ahead of him were shooting specialists Klay Thompson, Gary Trent Jr. and Landry Shamet.

articles.headline: Harry Maguire: Man United didn't take chances against Fulham, paid the price
articles.description: Harry Maguire said Manchester United paid the price for failing to take their chances in Sunday's 1-1 draw against Fulham.
articles.body:
Harry Maguire said Manchester United paid the price for failing to take their chances in Sunday's 1-1 draw against Fulham.

United were fortunate to leave west London with a point after Matheus Cunha's late deflected goal deceived goalkeeper Bernd Leno and denied Alvaro Arbeloa a first Premier League win in charge.

Sky Sports pundit Gary Neville branded the first 15 minutes of the second half, which culminated in a comical own goal from Lisandro Martínez to put Fulham in front, the worst he had seen in more than 45 years of watching the team play.

United hit a post in the first half through Bruno Fernandes, while Leno produced fine saves from Cunha, Martinez and Bryan Mbeumo.

"We have got to take our chances and take our moments," Maguire said to club media. "When you come away in the Premier League it is tough and you have seen that in the results this year.

"When we had those moments in that first half, they are big moments in the Premier League and you have really got to take them."

Fulham's goal went down against Martinez's name, but the blame was shared with his goalkeeper, a botched effort by Senne Lammens to shovel away Calvin Bassey's shot with his legs rather than his gloves, then an equally inexplicable and muddled attempt at keeping the defender's pass back to him out of his net.

The result means United have collected their joint fewest number of points after five matches in Premier League history.

Not since the 2014-15 season under Lous van Gaal have United picked up only five points by this stage and Carrick's class of 2026 will spend the extended international break in the bottom half of the table.

The team 11 years ago recovered from their poor start to eventually finish fourth and Maguire believes the current crop can kick on despite more dropped points.

"Our reaction was so much better and positive than it was last week [against Manchester City] and to concede that goal with the week we have had, the boys showed great spirit and great reaction," he said.

"We pushed them right back and the pressure was relentless. We needed a ball to fall or drop for us.

"It was just unfortunate that the goal did not come earlier as we had the momentum to go and win the match."

- Carrick has an impossible job at Man United after transfer failures

- Michael Carrick keen to find Man United positives, but there aren't many right now

- Carrick quashes notion Manchester United are out of shape

Cunha's 89th-minute shot hit defender David Affengruber and span cruelly past the wrong-footed Leno, with Fulham just minutes from victory.

It was, however, a muted, lethargic display from Carrick's team, who are now three league matches without a victory.

But Maguire said: "You have got to ignore the noise and really believe and think about what we have done this year, along with what we need to work on and improve on, but we are not far away."
